```python
import requests
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry

retry = Retry(total=3, backoff_factor=1, status_forcelist=[429, 500, 502, 503, 504])
session = requests.Session()
session.mount("https://", HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))
session.mount("http://", HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retry))

response = session.get("https://example.com/api", timeout=10)
```

This uses the retry support built into `requests`/`urllib3`, not a hand-written loop. It retries connection errors and the listed status codes up to three times, with the wait doubling each time (about 1s, 2s, 4s), then raises.

POST is not retried on those status codes by default because it is not idempotent; pass `allowed_methods=None` to `Retry` if your POSTs are safe to repeat.
